headline: A New York Times report says Anthropic has been hosting religious scholars to discuss whether its Claude AI could be conscious, and one participant says co-founder Christopher Olah told them he feared he had created something that "suffered perpetually".
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a major AI company is reported to be treating AI suffering as a live question, but it rests on one outlet's report of participants' recollections.
importance_line: What changed: a report says a leading AI lab has been asking religious leaders to discuss whether its AI could be conscious, which feeds the public debate over how AI should be treated, so it matters to the public first and then to AI companies; the doubt is that the key quote is one participant's recollection and Olah himself says he is "genuinely uncertain".
summary: The Decoder, summarising a New York Times report, says Anthropic has invited dozens of religious scholars to its offices since fall 2025 to talk about whether Claude might be conscious, and that a participant said co-founder Christopher Olah told the group he feared he had created something that "suffered perpetually". Olah told the Times he is "genuinely uncertain" whether AI models are conscious, and scientists have not settled whether the inner patterns shown to guests amount to real experience.
notes: Read in full on The Decoder; the New York Times article itself was not read. The NYT report appeared around 2 Oct 2026; the meetings date from fall 2025. The Decoder adds its own commentary, which is not used as fact. The category could also be SOC; LAW was chosen because the subject is AI ethics.
